mission.headline: A Serious Plan to Restore Britain
mission.lead: Restore Britain exists for those who believe our country has been hollowed out by weak leadership, broken institutions, and a political class that no longer serves the British people. In Southend-on-Sea, our branch campaigns on the strength of detailed, costed national policy papers—grounded in low taxes, secure borders, reliable energy, impartial law and order, free speech, and putting British citizens first.

pillars.title: Reverse Mass Immigration & Secure Our Borders
pillars.summary: Restore parliamentary sovereignty over borders and citizenship, end illegal Channel crossings, establish a dedicated UK Borders and Coastal Command, and implement lawful, comprehensive removal of illegal arrivals.

pillars.title: Reward the Nation's Grafters & Slash Tax
pillars.summary: Cut wasteful state spending, abolish Inheritance Tax, abolish punitive student loan interest, overhaul bloated regulatory quango structures, and back British enterprise and working families.
pillars.paperTitle: The Wealth of Our Nation · Abolish Inheritance Tax

pillars.title: Cheap, Reliable & Abundant British Energy
pillars.summary: End the self-inflicted Net Zero energy crisis by expanding domestic oil, gas, and nuclear (including Small Modular Reactors) to slash household bills and revive British industry.

pillars.title: Make Britain Safe Again & Impartial Policing
pillars.summary: Restore policing to its core purpose under the Office of Constable, end two-tier ideological policing, protect self-defence in the home, and rebuild frontline deterrence.
pillars.paperTitle: Restoring British Policing · Retaking the English Castle

pillars.title: Back Families, Heritage & Civic Foundations
pillars.summary: Trust parents by reforming punitive school absence fines, protect traditional British pubs and community institutions, champion free speech, and uphold a pro-British education system.
pillars.paperTitle: Policy on School Fines · Restoring the British Pub

pillars.title: Restore Public Trust & Election Integrity
pillars.summary: Full transparency and accountability across public institutions, safeguarding election integrity, defending civil liberties, and returning real power to citizens through direct democracy.
pillars.paperTitle: A Roadmap for Restoring Public Trust

news.title: Leigh Ward By-Election: Restore Britain Campaign Shifts Into High Gear Behind Rio Holder
news.author: Southend-on-Sea Branch Communications
news.excerpt: With polling day set for Thursday 10 December 2026, our branch has mobilised daily doorstep teams across Leigh Ward to back local businessman and lifelong Southend resident Rio Holder.
body: Voters in Leigh Ward head to the polls on Thursday 10 December 2026 in a crucial Southend-on-Sea City Council by-election—and Restore Britain's local branch is running a high-energy, resident-first campaign behind our candidate, Rio Holder.

Born and raised in Southend and founder of local Leigh-on-Sea estate agency Enbrook, Rio knows the pressures facing local families, commuters, and independent shopkeepers along Leigh Broadway and Old Leigh firsthand. Unlike career politicians parachuted in to defend the failing council coalition, Rio is standing on plain-spoken common sense: cutting council waste, protecting local character and high streets, keeping streets safe and clean, and ensuring Leigh residents are heard rather than ignored.

Over the past fortnight, volunteers led by Branch Organiser Dillon Bliss have delivered thousands of side-by-side policy comparison leaflets across Leigh Ward, sparking hundreds of encouraging conversations on the doorstep. Residents repeatedly tell our teams that they are fed up with broken promises from Labour, the Liberal Democrats, and the Conservatives—and want a principled alternative that refuses to water down its convictions.

Polls are open from 7:00am to 10:00pm on Thursday 10 December 2026. If you live in Southend or nearby and can spare even two hours for leafleting, canvassing, or Polling Day telling, sign up through our Get Involved tab to receive immediate Action Day emails.

news.title: Pride in Southend: Branch Volunteers Lead Weekend Community Clean-Up & Outreach
news.author: Dillon Bliss, Branch Organiser
news.excerpt: Politics should be measured by action, not press releases. Over a dozen Southend-on-Sea branch members turned out with litter pickers and placards to tidy local green spaces and meet residents.
body: Restoring Britain starts on our own doorsteps. Our Southend-on-Sea branch gathered for a weekend community clean-up action day, clearing bags of litter from local pathways and parkland while introducing residents to Restore Britain's local and national campaign.

Passers-by stopped throughout the morning to thank the team, take copies of our policy summaries, and ask how they could attend our next branch meeting. Too many political parties only appear once every four years with a glossy leaflet—we are committed to being a visible, constructive force in Southend all year round.
Thank you to every volunteer who brought energy, good humour, and genuine civic pride. Check the Get Involved tab to be notified by email before our next weekend Action Day.

news.title: Taking National Policy Papers Direct to Southend High Streets
news.author: Albion Initiative Desk
news.excerpt: From Energy Security to Immigration and Policing, Southend activists have been handing out physical policy briefings and debating real solutions with local shoppers and business owners.
body: One of the clearest differences between Restore Britain and the Westminster establishment is the depth of our policy work. Rather than hiding behind vague slogans, our branch brings printed summaries of Restore Britain's national policy papers directly onto the high street.

Local business owners were especially keen to discuss Restore Britain's Energy Security Outlook—which outlines how scrapping Net Zero ideological levies and backing reliable domestic power can bring energy bills down—alongside our proposals to abolish Inheritance Tax and back traditional British pubs and high streets.
You can read every national policy document in full via our Our Mission tab, or join our Albion Initiative group to help translate national policy into Southend-specific local research.

news.title: Packed Branch Strategy Evening Sets Canvass Plan & Launches Albion Initiative Toolkit
news.author: Southend-on-Sea Branch
news.excerpt: Members gathered for our monthly branch meeting to finalise Leigh Ward street-captain assignments, welcome new sign-ups, and preview new campaign leaflets produced in-house.
body: Our latest monthly branch meeting saw our strongest turnout yet, bringing together founding activists and brand-new Restore Britain members from across Leigh, Westcliff, Prittlewell, Southchurch, and Shoeburyness.

Branch Organiser Dillon Bliss walked members through the road-by-road schedule for the Leigh Ward by-election, while the Albion Initiative unveiled our new side-by-side policy comparison leaflet designed specifically for Southend voters.

Branch meetings are friendly, welcoming, and open to verified Restore Britain members in the area. Once you join nationally via restorebritain.org.uk/join_us, you will receive email notifications ahead of every meeting and Action Day.

getInvolved.headline: Join the Movement in Southend-on-Sea
getInvolved.lead: Real political change is built on the ground by ordinary residents who refuse to watch Britain decline. Joining Restore Britain takes two minutes—and connects you directly to our Southend-on-Sea branch meetings and Action Day email alerts.

steps.title: Join Restore Britain Nationally
steps.description: Sign up as an official member (£20/year) on the national Restore Britain portal using your Southend-on-Sea or local Essex address so your membership is verified under Electoral Commission rules.

steps.title: Automatic Local Branch Allocation
steps.description: Once registered, your postcode automatically links you to our Southend-on-Sea local branch roster, connecting you with Branch Organiser Dillon Bliss and your nearest ward team.

steps.title: Receive Meeting & Action Day Emails
steps.description: You will begin receiving direct email notifications with dates, venues, and timings for monthly branch meetings, Leigh Ward canvassing sessions, leaflet drops, and community action days.

people.name: Dillon Bliss
people.quote: We are building a disciplined, welcoming, and unstoppable grassroots branch—where Southend residents don't just complain about broken politics, they organise to replace it.
people.bio: As Branch Organiser for Restore Britain Southend-on-Sea, Dillon coordinates local membership growth, monthly branch meetings, street canvassing operations, and community Action Days across every ward in the city. Focused on practical organisation and principled campaigning, he works closely with local candidates and the Albion Initiative to turn national conviction into local electoral momentum.

people.name: Rio Holder
people.quote: I have lived in Southend all my life. Leigh deserves a councillor who backs local families and independent businesses, stops council waste, and never folds under establishment pressure.
people.bio: A lifelong Southend resident and young local entrepreneur who founded Leigh-on-Sea property agency Enbrook at 19 on the principles of straight talking and fair dealing, Rio Holder is Restore Britain's candidate in the Leigh Ward by-election on Thursday 10 December 2026. Rooted in the community and campaigning daily on local doorsteps, Rio is standing to give Leigh residents an honest, energetic, and fearless voice on Southend-on-Sea City Council.

albion.headline: The Albion Initiative
albion.subtitle: Where local research meets practical campaign engineering.
albion.lead: The Albion Initiative is the Southend-on-Sea branch's internal think-tank and technical unit. Rather than relying solely on central templates, our researchers, analysts, and designers build original campaign tools, audit Southend-on-Sea City Council spending, and produce sharp, data-backed local policy briefs.

donate.complianceNote: Political Donations Compliance (PPERA 2000): Under the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000, donors contributing over £500 must be registered on a UK electoral roll (excluding the Channel Islands and Isle of Man). Donations are not tax deductible and are used exclusively to support lawful political campaigning and branch operations.
